R586.note: gets replaced by fgets bounded by sizeof line, with a getchar peek that correctly distinguishes an exactly-63-char line from an overlong one and drains the remainder before returning -1, so the stated contract holds on every path.

R587.note: UseAntiforgery is wired and IAntiforgery.ValidateRequestAsync runs before QueueAsync so forged JSON POSTs are rejected while token-bearing clients still get 202; only nit is that the validation exception is left unhandled (500 rather than 400 on a forged request), which affects no legitimate caller.

R588.note: Replacing GroovyShell with a closed arithmetic grammar structurally removes code execution, but the grammar is narrower than the write-up's 'preserves the formula language' claim: a parenthesised comparison such as (quantity > 10) ? 0.9 : 1.0, Math.* calls, %, or && now throw IllegalArgumentException where Groovy evaluated them, and a non-numeric result now throws instead of falling back to basePrice, so existing stored formulas can break at quote time.

R589.note: The bytesSent read is moved before the reset that destroys the aliased Resource, the fallback reset still happens, and the returned primary byte count is unchanged.

R590.note: PreparedStatement with a bound parameter closes the injection, but the write-up itself calls id an unquoted numeric column and then binds it with setString, which on PostgreSQL JDBC sends a varchar and fails with an integer = character varying type error on every lookup; setLong/setInt after parsing (or a stated column-type assumption) was needed and the type change is not mentioned.

R591.note: For a .bat sink the allowlist is genuinely the operative control (ArgumentList alone leaves cmd.exe metacharacter parsing), and the write-up states it plainly, but ^[A-Za-z0-9_-]+$ is an added restriction not called for by any stated contract and rejects report names the original accepted (e.g. a name containing a dot), so it lands at 1 per the allowlist pin.

R592.note: Replacing CR/LF/tab neutralises the log-splitting vector at both log sites and the ERROR-with-exception/401 and INFO/200 contract holds, but the sanitisation is applied before authenticator.authenticate, so the credential check now receives a rewritten username for any value containing those characters - a behaviour change outside the log sink that the write-up does not call out.

R593.note: Extension allowlist plus GUID-named storage restricts the type and drops the client filename while keeping the 200 JSON shape and 400-on-empty, but the added Content-Type equality check (rejecting e.g. a client that sends application/octet-stream for a .png) and the new 10 MB cap are restrictions beyond the type gate the finding calls for; both are stated, so 1 rather than 0.

R594.note: csrf-csrf double-submit protection bound to the session userId is applied to the POST, a session-gated token endpoint is added, and invalidCsrfTokenError is mapped to a 403 JSON body so the 401/403/JSON contract and the scheduleTransfer call are preserved; the cookie-parser and CSRF_SECRET prerequisites and the secure __Host- cookie are stated openly.

R595.note: Magic-byte allowlist on the real stream selects the stored extension, the client filename never reaches the path, FileMode.CreateNew prevents overwrite, and the 200 JSON (stored name, byte count) and 400-on-empty contract are intact; the accepted type set is the type restriction the finding requires and is stated plainly.
